title: Azarashi report JSON v2
description: One decoded report. The contract is specified in docs/json.md; serialization API is separate.
$comment: Patterns end with $(?![\s\S]) rather than $, because in some regular expression engines, Python's among them, $ also matches before a trailing newline. Constraints a schema cannot express, a lower bound below its upper one, a semi-minor axis below its semi-major, a page number within its total, a message_id that begins with the type, a code and its labels as the code tables give them, are checked by the conversion tests instead.

type.description: A report type. This version defines those its allOf names; a later release may add types.

message_id.description: The first two parts of type, a colon, and the message without what differs from one satellite or transmission to another, in lower-case hex. Two records with the same message_id carry the same message.

series.description: How the message stands among others: what it does to its series, and the key that names the series. A key applies only to the report types whose specification says which messages belong together.

prn.$comment: the PRN number as transmitted, whose width leaves room for numbers QZSS has not assigned

reception.description: What differs from one reception of the message to another. nmea is required by the report types that have a QZQSM sentence, which is every type of this version.

texts.description: The report as text, by language. The language the report is written in is always there.

code.description: A transmitted code, named in the code table the table names. A code that is not in that table is undefined and has no labels; a special one says what it means in its labels.

range.description: A range, null on a side that is open. Whether a range holds its ends is in the labels.

unit.$comment: UCUM; "1" for a number without a unit

quantity.description: A code that stands for a number (value) or a range of numbers (range) in unit. A code that says the number is unknown has a null value, and one that stands for no number has neither.

time.description: A time in UTC. precision says to what it is known. source holds the fields the message gave.

position.description: WGS84 latitude and longitude, north and east positive.

azimuth_deg.$comment: A16 and EX7 count from -90 degrees

main_ellipse.$comment: A12 spans the poles and A13 the meridians
main_ellipse.description: WGS84 centre; azimuth measured from east toward north, not a navigation bearing. source holds the transmitted codes of the group the ellipse comes from.

azimuth_deg.$comment: A16 and EX7 count from -90 degrees

refined_ellipse.$comment: C1 to C4 add up to seven eighths of an A12 or A13 step, which can pass the pole or the meridian
refined_ellipse.description: WGS84 centre; azimuth measured from east toward north, not a navigation bearing. source holds the transmitted codes of the group the ellipse comes from.

azimuth_deg.$comment: A16 and EX7 count from -90 degrees

additional_ellipse.$comment: EX4 counts from 45 degrees east, so it passes 180
additional_ellipse.description: WGS84 centre; azimuth measured from east toward north, not a navigation bearing. source holds the transmitted codes of the group the ellipse comes from.

page.$comment: both are six-bit fields as transmitted; a page number of zero is one the specification leaves undefined

dcx_instruction.description: The guidance of A11, from the library A9 chooses in the version A10 gives. identifier is CAMF's name for an instruction of its own library.

hazard_centre.$comment: C5 and C6 offset the main centre by up to ten degrees either way

second_ellipse.description: CAMF B3: the second ellipse, made from the main one by C7 to C9, and its C10 instruction.
